subject: Pilot amendment: extension and performance-slabs
messages:
From: Evan Lewis <evan@hallowayhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline — need a short extension?

Hi Michael,

Quick one — our security team just kicked off an extra compliance checklist for the pilot that will delay our data onboarding by ~10 business days. We want to keep momentum but need to avoid the pilot lapsing while we finish the checklist.

Can Redwood either (a) add two weeks to the pilot timeline at the same price, or (b) provide some form of performance credit if we opt to keep the original end date? Procurement is leaning toward option (b) but wants specific mechanics.

Also looping procurement in case they want to handle contractual language: procurement@hallowayhealth.com

Thanks,
Evan Lewis
Head of Integrations
Halloway Health


From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Evan Lewis <evan@hallowayhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline — need a short extension?

Thanks for the heads up, Evan — sorry to hear the compliance queue popped. We can do this a couple ways; I outlined two practical options below so procurement has something concrete to react to.

Option A — Time extension
- Add 14 calendar days to the pilot term; no price change, no modifications to deliverables.
- Existing SLA and support scope remain unchanged.
- We can amend with a short addendum (2–3 lines).

Option B — Performance-slabs (credit-based) — keeps original end date
- Redwood applies an invoice credit if the service meets defined performance targets during a one-week stretch-window near the end of the pilot.
- Proposed metric set (draft): 99th-pct latency < 150ms for gen calls; successful request rate >= 99.5%; sustained throughput >= 50 tokens/sec for the workload pattern in your metrics file.
- If all targets are met during the window, Halloway receives a credit equal to 15% of the pilot fees (applied to the first paid invoice after pilot). Partial attainment scales the credit linearly (e.g., 2/3 targets => 10% credit).
- We can make this both measurable and auditable — we’ll provide per-token logs and a short joint measurement window.

I attached a short draft amendment for either path and a metrics template we can fill with your engineering team. If procurement prefers a single-number extension, pick A. If you want to hedge and keep the original end date, B is a common approach we use.

Attached: pilot-amendment-draft.pdf; halloway-eval-metrics.xlsx

Happy to hop on a 15-min call to run through — Kimberly / David, can one of you take point if Evan wants to finalize?

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Evan Lewis <evan@hallowayhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Halloway Health Procurement <procurement@hallowayhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline — need a short extension?

Thanks Michael — useful framing. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement/ops before we loop engineering:

1) For Option B, is the credit issued as a line-item credit on our invoice (applied forward) or as a retroactive rebate you pay out? Procurement prefers credit applied to our next invoice.
2) Can you confirm how the measurement window is selected and who owns the logging — we need an auditable trail for our compliance records.
3) If we choose B and miss targets by a small margin, what dispute route do we have? E.g., review period with your team and joint verification.

Procurement note: we will need contract language that (a) defines the measurement window, (b) specifies evidence required, and (c) caps credits so finance can model worst-case.

Evan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Evan Lewis <evan@hallowayhealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline — need a short extension?

Evan — thanks, we talked this morning and I pushed the draft into a version that addresses procurement concerns. Key points in the attached amendment (pilot-amendment-draft.pdf):

- Measurement window: 7-consecutive-calendar-day window selected jointly by Halloway and Redwood; window must begin no later than three business days before the pilot end date unless both parties agree otherwise.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide request-level logs (token counts, timestamps, response latencies, and error codes). Halloway may provide its own sampled telemetry.
- Credit mechanics: Applied as an invoice credit on the next Redwood invoice; credit capped at 20% of pilot fees to limit finance exposure. Partial attainment prorated.
- Dispute & verification: 5-business-day review period after the measurement window; if parties cannot agree, an independent third-party (mutually agreed) can be engaged; costs split 50/50 and capped at $5k.
- Implementation: If you want B we’ll record the measurement parameters in the amendment and hit DocuSign. If you want A, the amendment is shorter and also attached.

Attached: pilot-amendment-draft.pdf (amendment v1.1), halloway-eval-metrics.xlsx

DocuSign (if you’re ready): https://docusign.com/XYZ-3456

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0120

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Evan Lewis <evan@hallowayhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline — need a short extension?

Thanks all — finance/legal ran the cap and credit wording and are OK with the amendment as-is. A couple operational items from our side:

- Credit application: confirmed as invoice credit on the next Redwood invoice; we’ll include a line referencing DEAL-8813 for tracking.
- PO/line-item: Evan / procurement, can you confirm the PO number or remit-to entity so finance records the credit correctly?
- Timeline: if you pick Option B, please review the amendment and sign via the DocuSign link by EOD Mon 6/7 so we can schedule the joint measurement window. If you pick Option A, we’ll sign the short addendum and we’ll extend the pilot by 14 days immediately upon countersignature.

Short call is fine if anyone prefers to resolve quickly — I can take Wed morning next week.

David Kim
Director, Customer Finance Operations
redwood_finance@redwood.com
